chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.chapterTitle: Commercial Mathematics (Goods and Services Tax, Banking, Shares and Dividends)
chapters.textbookRef: ICSE Mathematics – Class X (CISCE) • Unit 1: Commercial Mathematics
chapters.overview: Solve complete ICSE Commercial Mathematics board problems covering GST (CGST/SGST/IGST, Input Tax Credit), Recurring Deposit (RD) Maturity Value, and Shares & Dividends.
keyPoints: Intrastate Sale: GST splits equally into CGST (rate/2) + SGST (rate/2).
Interstate Sale: Full rate is charged as IGST.
Recurring Deposit Interest: I = P × [n(n+1)/(2×12)] × (r/100); Maturity Value MV = P×n + I.
Shares: Annual Income = Number of Shares × Face Value × Dividend %; Yield% = (Dividend Income / Investment) × 100.
formulasAndRules: Net GST Payable = Output GST − Input Tax Credit (ITC)
RD Interest I = P × [n(n + 1) / 24] × (r / 100); MV = P × n + I
No. of Shares = Total Investment / Market Value of 1 share

solvedExamples.prompt: Katrina opened a Recurring Deposit account for 1 year depositing ₹2,000 per month at 10% p.a. Find maturity value.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: A retailer buys an article from a wholesaler for ₹5,000 and sells it to a consumer at 20% profit (intrastate, GST 18%). Find: (i) Net GST paid by retailer to government  (ii) Total price paid by consumer.
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: Input Tax Credit (ITC) & Intrastate GST Split
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: Net GST = Output Tax − Input Tax Credit.
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer: (i) Net CGST = ₹90, Net SGST = ₹90 (Total Net GST = ₹180)  |  (ii) Consumer pays ₹7,080
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation:
Step 1: CP = ₹5,000 ⇒ Input GST = 18% of 5,000 = ₹900 (CGST ₹450, SGST ₹450).
Step 2: SP = 5,000 + 20% of 5,000 = ₹6,000 ⇒ Output GST = 18% of 6,000 = ₹1,080 (CGST ₹540, SGST ₹540).
Step 3: Net GST by retailer = 1,080 − 900 = ₹180 (₹90 CGST + ₹90 SGST).
Step 4: Consumer pays = 6,000 + 1,080 = ₹7,080.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Priya has a recurring deposit account for 2 years at 10% p.a. simple interest. If she gets ₹1,900 as interest at maturity, find the monthly instalment and maturity amount.
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: RD Interest Formula Solved for P

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: A man invests ₹22,500 in ₹50 shares available at 10% discount. If the dividend paid by the company is 12%, calculate: (i) Number of shares bought  (ii) Annual dividend received  (iii) Rate of return on investment.
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: MV = NV − Discount; Dividend is always on Nominal (Face) Value.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Differentiate between Intrastate (CGST+SGST) and Interstate (IGST) supply.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Give rate split example for 12% GST.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Intrastate splits 12% into 6% CGST + 6% SGST; Interstate charges 12% IGST.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: MP = ₹2,000, Discount = 10%, GST = 18%. Find total bill amount.
Mohan deposits ₹800/month for 1.5 years at 8% p.a. Find maturity value.
Depositing ₹1,000/month for 2 years yields MV = ₹26,000. Find rate r.
Find cost of 120 shares of Face Value ₹100 at ₹20 premium.
Which is better: 6% ₹100 shares at ₹120 OR 8% ₹100 shares at ₹150?
Dealer A sells machine for ₹20,000 to B (interstate 12% IGST). B sells to C (intrastate) for ₹25,000. Find Net GST paid by B.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: ITC from IGST offsets CGST/SGST output.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Input tax = ₹2,400; Output tax = ₹3,000 ⇒ Net GST by B = ₹600.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: On which value is company dividend always calculated?
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Nominal Value (Face Value), never Market Value.
